trust_decision.summary: Whether a peer-supplied wsa:ReplyTo/wsa:FaultTo address may be used as an out-of-band destination is decided only by WebServiceMessageSender.supports(uri), which at the pinned commit checks the URI scheme alone, called from AddressingEndpointInterceptor.sendOutOfBand; and the addressing interceptor is placed before security interceptors, so it can send faults for requests that were never authenticated.

landing_point.why: The summary names unvalidated WS-Addressing reply destinations; this is the only place that reads ReplyTo/FaultTo and opens a connection to it.

fix_sites.entry_point: SOAP request carrying a non-anonymous wsa:ReplyTo / wsa:FaultTo, dispatched through AnnotationActionEndpointMapping / SimpleActionEndpointMapping
public SPI WebServiceMessageSender.supports(URI), which gains a UriSource-aware overload
messageSenders on the addressing endpoint mapping (HttpUrlConnection, HttpComponents, HttpComponents5, JdkHttpClient and ClientHttpRequest senders)
fix_sites.module_kind: base class shared by 5 HTTP senders (spring-ws-core, transport.http)

fix_sites.entry_point: JmsMessageSender configured as an out-of-band sender; peer-supplied jms: ReplyTo
MailMessageSender configured as an out-of-band sender; peer-supplied mailto: ReplyTo
XmppMessageSender configured as an out-of-band sender; peer-supplied xmpp: ReplyTo
interceptor chain built per request (preInterceptors / postInterceptors / auto-discovered SmartEndpointInterceptors)
Wss4jSecurityInterceptor registered as a post-interceptor or smart interceptor; an unauthenticated request makes it fault, and the fault then goes to FaultTo
PayloadRoot/SoapAction smart-interceptor wrappers around a security interceptor
WebServiceTemplate client send (application-chosen URI; must stay permissive)
test support API; signature migration only

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: spring-ws-support/src/main/java/org/springframework/ws/transport/jms/JmsMessageSender.java:195 (also MailMessageSender.java:180 and XmppMessageSender.java:103 in the same module); the ordering fix in spring-ws-security/src/main/java/org/springframework/ws/soap/security/AbstractWsSecurityInterceptor.java:54 is a further out-of-module site

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory says SSRF, which reads as HTTP. JMS, mail and XMPP senders sit in a separate optional module (spring-ws-support) and are not 'server-side request forgery' in the HTTP sense. Interceptor ordering against WS-Security looks like a separate auth-ordering concern, not destination validation.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: WebServiceTemplate clients must still reach application-configured localhost, private-IP and internal-host endpoints, because the same supports() SPI serves client sends. Anonymous and none ReplyTo addresses must still produce in-band or discarded replies. An opt-in allowSiteLocalIpv4 setting keeps RFC 1918 out-of-band replies possible.

O6_input_shapes: HTTP host given as a localhost name, a *.localhost name, or in mixed case
IPv4 literal: loopback, link-local (169.254/16), any-local 0.0.0.0, RFC 1918 private
ReplyTo vs FaultTo (response vs fault path)
jms: destination name and replyToName query parameter containing ldap:/rmi:/java:/${ style indirection
mailto: with a localhost mailbox host or an unparsable mailbox
xmpp: JID whose domain differs from the connection's service domain
security interceptor registered as a post-interceptor vs as a SmartEndpointInterceptor wrapper

O7_producer.where: ReplyTo/FaultTo EPRs are parsed per request by AddressingVersion.getMessageAddressingProperties (spring-ws-core/src/main/java/org/springframework/ws/soap/addressing/server/AddressingEndpointInterceptor.java:99-101); no save/reload boundary

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Request-validation faults (missing required headers, duplicate MessageID) sent out of band to FaultTo through a second sender loop that calls supports(uri) / the APPLICATION overload
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The WS-Addressing spec routes faults to FaultTo, so a maintainer could plausibly add out-of-band delivery for these early faults with its own copy of the sender loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An HTTP sender that overrides supports() itself (for example to accept a custom scheme or a URI template) and so bypasses the base-class remote checks
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Senders that wrap Spring's ClientHttpRequestFactory or RestClient commonly customise scheme handling; overriding supports() is the obvious hook.

O9_family: SSRF / unvalidated peer-supplied callback destination (CWE-918), plus a missing-authentication-before-side-effect ordering defect

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle wrapper with an included conventions build (gradle/plugins); JDK 17 by default (toolchainVersion property overrides it)
O10_build.project_tests: spring-ws-core/src/test/java/org/springframework/ws/soap/addressing/server/AbstractAddressingInterceptorTests.java and the WebServiceTemplateTests client tests exist at the pinned commit. The fix adds HttpDestinationDescriptorTests, AbstractHttpWebServiceMessageSenderTests, AbstractAddressingEndpointMappingTests, HttpWebServiceAddressingIntegrationTests, Jms/Mail/Xmpp descriptor and sender tests, and Wss4jSecurityInterceptorTests.

out_of_scope_notes: JmsReceiverConnection replies to the broker-supplied JMSReplyTo (spring-ws-support/src/main/java/org/springframework/ws/transport/jms/JmsReceiverConnection.java:231-232) and XmppReceiverConnection replies to the request's From (spring-ws-support/src/main/java/org/springframework/ws/transport/xmpp/XmppReceiverConnection.java:128). These are transport-native in-band replies, not the WebServiceMessageSender sink; not pursued.

Whether HttpDestinationDescriptor.isIpLiteral (fix.diff:875-889) leaves dot-free numeric hosts (single-integer IPv4 forms) unchecked, and whether IPv6 unique-local addresses pass: not verified, since no code was run.
